description: This news report, published by The Guardian on 21 April 2023 and republished by the European Council for an Energy Efficient Economy, describes the community solar microgrid built by the environmental group Casa Pueblo in Adjuntas, Puerto Rico. Nearly 700 rooftop solar panels serve 14 local businesses, among them a pharmacy and a bakery, and the microgrid can run independently of the island's fossil-fuelled grid to provide backup during outages while staying connected to the national network to cut costs. Casa Pueblo's headquarters kept power during Hurricane Maria in 2017 because it already had solar panels and batteries, and Hurricane Fiona later damaged infrastructure again. Coverage is one town, and the article is free to read without a stated licence. The source is a web article available online. Caveats: it is journalism with no technical data, the panel count is approximate and outcomes are quoted from the director. For simulation, it offers an example for resilience and capacity planning of community microgrids in hurricane zones.
